1.why: The interface uses a clean sans-serif typeface with adequate line spacing, though the spacing is standard rather than notably generous.

2.why: Instruction text throughout uses short plain lines with no italics, no all-caps, and no dense blocks (the all-caps '[TEST ONLY]' text appears only in the Logs panel, not in instructions).

3.why: All provided screenshots are desktop-width views of a centered single-column card, so readability at an actual mobile screen size cannot be confirmed from the evidence.

4.why: Instructions are one to two short sentences in mostly plain language, with only mild jargon such as 'setup secret' and 'browser developer console'.

5.why: Format examples appear as placeholders for the mobile number ('+15551234567') and recovery code ('ABCD-EFGH-IJKL') and the label '6-digit verification code' states the format, but the authenticator code field has no example.

6.why: No step requires reading more than two short sentences; the only long text (the Logs panel) is not required reading to proceed.

7.why: The setup secret and recovery codes are rendered as ordinary selectable text that can be copied, although no dedicated copy button is provided.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent is shown anywhere; step 4 explicitly tells the user to 'add it manually to your authenticator app'.

9.why: The form fields look like standard inputs, but nothing in the screenshots confirms or denies browser autofill or password manager support.

10.why: Each step has a large bold heading naming the current step and a high-contrast blue primary button, though the Logs panel and the multi-button settings page slightly compete for attention.

11.why: Every enrolment step presents a single primary action, but the MFA settings screen simultaneously offers three actions (verify, regenerate, log out).

12.why: Some actions get plain confirmations ('Recovery code accepted and used.', 'MFA is enabled. 8 recovery codes remain.'), but sending the verification code merely adds an input field, with the confirmation appearing only in the Logs panel.

13.why: The user can retry after an error ('Please try again'), re-send the verification code, and regenerate recovery codes with no visible penalty, though no reveal/hide toggles for codes are shown.

14.why: The only observed error, 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.', does not state what the problem is, offering only a generic retry suggestion without blame.

15.why: No timers, countdowns, or session limits are visible on any screen, so nothing indicates time pressure on reading or code entry.
